correctness.rationale: The matrix powers are exact; C mod2 nonzero establishes the least period by repeated doubling. The base zero list modulo 8 and the C derivative leave 2+1 nonsingular zero classes. In the singular class, f(t) modulo 16 forces t=4s. The expansion g(s)=580+d2(s-1)+8h(s), d2 odd, h 1-Lipschitz, implies an isometry with one odd 2-adic root. Two separate s-classes modulo 2^(k-5) each have four lifts in the period for k>=6. Complete residue enumeration k<=12 and independent matrix computations corroborate arithmetic input; they are not substituted for the infinite proof. Scope includes n=0; no limit approximation.

value.rationale: The exact number of zero residues in a least modular period is a natural local invariant that is not determined by the already-tabulated period lengths. The surprising 11-count stabilizes from exponent six onwards, despite exponentially growing periods. The proof explains the structural eight-plus-three split via one singular 2-adic analytic branch and two nonsingular Hensel branches, giving a meaningful infinite exact classification rather than arbitrary finite enumeration.
